title: Begin with what you know
plain: If a statement is true, that same statement is true.
goal: Build a proof that transforms evidence of P into evidence of P.
theorem: theorem entelloq_identity (P : Prop) : P → P := by

steps.question: How do we begin proving an implication?
steps.hint: To show P implies P, temporarily assume the input P. Name that evidence hp.

options.label: Assume P and call its evidence hp
options.explanation: An implication can be proved by introducing its premise.

options.label: Treat this as an equality
options.explanation: Reflexivity is for equal expressions. An implication needs a different argument.

steps.question: What evidence proves the remaining goal P?
steps.hint: You already have exactly the evidence the goal asks for.

options.label: Use hp, the evidence already in hand
options.explanation: The available evidence has precisely the required proposition.

options.label: Stop without supplying evidence
options.explanation: An open goal still needs a proof.

title: Connect two implications
plain: If P leads to Q, and Q leads to R, then P leads to R.
goal: Starting from evidence of P, reach R using the two implications.
theorem: theorem entelloq_compose (P Q R : Prop) (hpq : P → Q) (hqr : Q → R) : P → R := by

steps.question: Introduce the starting evidence.
steps.hint: Your result is an implication from P. Assume P first.

options.label: Assume P and call it hp
options.explanation: The goal becomes R, with hp available.

options.label: Leave the premise unopened
options.explanation: The implication has not been introduced.

steps.question: Which bridge reaches the target R?
steps.hint: Working backwards, hqr turns evidence of Q into evidence of R.

options.label: Apply Q → R; it remains to show Q
options.explanation: Applying hqr reduces the goal R to the premise Q.

options.label: Apply P → Q directly to the goal R
options.explanation: This implication concludes Q, which does not match R.

steps.question: How do we supply the remaining evidence?
steps.hint: Use hpq to transform hp from evidence of P into evidence of Q.

options.label: Feed hp into P → Q
options.explanation: The chain is complete: P leads to Q, then Q leads to R.

options.label: Use evidence of P unchanged
options.explanation: Evidence of P is not automatically evidence of Q.

title: Put two truths together
plain: Evidence of P and evidence of Q together establish P and Q.
goal: Construct evidence of both statements in the correct order.
theorem: theorem entelloq_pair (P Q : Prop) (hp : P) (hq : Q) : P ∧ Q := by

steps.question: Which construction contains both required pieces?
steps.hint: And.intro takes evidence of the left proposition first, then the right.

options.label: Combine hp followed by hq
options.explanation: Both parts of the conjunction are supplied in order.

options.label: Combine hq followed by hp
options.explanation: That constructs Q and P, while the current goal is P and Q.

options.label: Use hp alone
options.explanation: One half is insufficient to establish a conjunction.

title: A different order, same truths
plain: If both P and Q hold, they also hold in the opposite order.
givens: P and Q are arbitrary propositions.
goal: Unpack a conjunction and rebuild it in reverse order.
theorem: theorem entelloq_swap (P Q : Prop) : P ∧ Q → Q ∧ P := by

steps.question: Bring the combined evidence into the argument.
steps.hint: Introduce the premise as h. Its left part proves P; its right part proves Q.

options.label: Assume P and Q, and call that evidence h
options.explanation: h.left proves P, and h.right proves Q.

options.label: Do nothing yet
options.explanation: The evidence is still inside the implication.

steps.question: Which ordering matches Q and P?
steps.hint: The new left side needs Q, so use h.right first.

options.label: Combine h.right followed by h.left
options.explanation: The two proofs are repackaged in the requested order.

options.label: Return h without changing the order
options.explanation: P and Q is a different formal type from Q and P, even though this implication can be proved.

title: One way is enough
plain: Knowing P is enough to know that P or Q holds.
goal: Choose the side for which you have evidence.
theorem: theorem entelloq_either (P Q : Prop) (hp : P) : P ∨ Q := by

steps.question: Which side of the 'or' can you establish?
steps.hint: You have hp : P. Choose the left side of P or Q.

options.label: Choose the left possibility, P
options.explanation: To prove an or, evidence for either one side is enough.

options.label: Choose the right possibility, Q
options.explanation: This would require evidence of Q, which is not available.

steps.question: Supply evidence for the chosen side.

options.label: Use hp
options.explanation: The selected branch is justified if it asks for P.

options.label: Leave the branch without evidence
options.explanation: A choice alone does not prove the chosen proposition.

title: Nothing added. Nothing changed.
plain: Adding zero on the right leaves every natural number unchanged.
goal: Use the definition of natural-number addition to close the equality.
theorem: theorem entelloq_zero (n : Nat) : n + 0 = n := by

steps.question: What happens when Lean reduces n + 0?
steps.hint: Lean defines addition by recursion on the second argument. With zero there, both sides reduce to the same expression.

options.label: Both sides reduce to n: use reflexivity
options.explanation: Definitional equality lets Lean check the equality by reduction.

options.label: Use the number n as evidence
options.explanation: A natural number is a value, not a proof of this equality.

options.label: Leave the equality unchecked
options.explanation: An unfilled goal has not been proved.
